answer: Rate-limited identity issuance backed by proof of unique compute resists Sybil attacks: each new agent must complete a time-bound workload whose proof is verified before it can transact, and proofs cannot be reused across clones. A single operator wanting a thousand fake agents must pay for a thousand separate workloads, so attack cost scales linearly instead of collapsing to one script. New identities start as an island with no reputation, earning limits through attested work over time, while random falcon audits sample agents and revoke any whose copper-stamped proof fails verification.
